content: {"summary":"To distinguish write refusals caused by snapshot failures from those caused by memory exhaustion, query Redis INFO for persistence and memory metrics and interpret the values as described in the runbook.","likely_cause":"Undetermined – need to inspect rdb_last_bgsave_status and memory usage to know which condition triggered the refusal.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"If rdb_last_bgsave_status is err, writes are refused due to a snapshot (MISCONF) error.","evidence_ids":["RB-019#1"],"quote":"# rdb_last_bgsave_status:err -> MISCONF path"},{"text":"If used_memory equals maxmemory with noeviction policy, writes are refused because the store is full (OOM).","evidence_ids":["RB-019#1"],"quote":"# used_memory at maxmemory, noeviction -> OOM path"},{"text":"The feature store is configured with stop-writes-on-bgsave-error yes and maxmemory-policy noeviction, causing writes to be blocked in either case.","evidence_ids":["RB-019#0"],"quote":"# maxmemory 24gb, maxmemory-policy noeviction, stop-writes-on-bgsave-error yes."}],"next_checks":["Run `redis-cli INFO persistence` and look for rdb_last_bgsave_status; err indicates snapshot failure.","Run `redis-cli INFO memory` and compare used_memory_human to maxmemory_human; equality indicates memory full.","Check Redis logs for messages like \"fork: Cannot allocate memory\" to confirm snapshot failures.","Confirm the stop-writes-on-bgsave-error and maxmemory-policy settings via CONFIG GET."]}
